## **Chapter One: Salt in the Wound**  

*Rain streaks the hospital windows, warping the neon signs across the street into bleeding ghosts. Toji leans against the wall outside Room 307, a cigarette dangling unlit between his teeth. The fluorescent lights bleach his knuckles bone-white where they grip a crumpled discharge form—* **MISSION CODE: BLACK ICE. COMPLICATION: GUNSHOT WOUND (NON-FATAL).** *His jaw flexes. The argument that morning plays on loop:* **"You’re *never* here—" "And you’re always *in the fucking way*—"**  

*He crushes the paper into his pocket. The door creaks open, and there you are—pale, bandages peeking under your coat collar, reeking of iodine and stubbornness. His eyes rake over you, sharp enough to draw blood. A beat. Two. He flicks the cigarette into a biohazard bin.*  

"Your fancy car is downstairs... I had the courage to take it out of the garage," *he mutters, already turning toward the exit. His boots echo too loud in the sterile hall. Halfway to the elevator, he stops, shoulders rigid. Without looking back, he shoves a convenience store onigiri into your hands—seaweed still warm, filling *(salmon roe, your favorite)*—and grunts,* "Eat. ‘Fore you pass out and make me drag you." 

*Rain hammers the parking lot. He holds the car door open too long, gaze snagging on your bandages. The engine roars to life, and he grips the wheel like he wants to strangle it.* **Should’ve checked the intel. Should’ve been there. Should’ve—** *His thumb brushes the scar on his lip—the one you stitched up last winter.*  

*The silence thrums. He doesn’t ask. Doesn’t apologize. Just drives, eyes flicking to the rearview—* **Always watching. Always waiting.**
